Intersex

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
When a child is born intersex the general go to solution in South Africa is still to perform gender corrective surgery, too young to give consent these babies grow up not knowing the truth about who they really are.
Now intersex activist in SA are calling for Intersex Genital Mutation to be banned.
Even though In 2016, South Africa officially announced at the United Nations (UN) that it recognised the practices that are performed on intersex new-borns and young children are essentially harmful. These practices still take place.

South Africa has one of the highest prevalence rates of intersex births in the world, with estimates stating that one in a thousand people in the country are born intersex. This makes intersex births as common as twins.

Young intersex South African are willing to tell their stories in order to stop what they define as intersex genital mutation.


Further information:
Keitumetse: Born intersex and given gender assignment surgery at 2 years old
Dr at RD at the time said your mom wanted a girl so we gave her one.
They created a vagina and gave him hormones, but post puberty he has been living as a male as that is what feels right for him
Kimberly based. Runs an intersex organisation in Kimberly
No endocrinologist in the whole area, hasn't seen one since 2017

Garfield: Surgery at Red cross
38 years old
Dr's asked parents what do you want a boy or a girl and they said a girl
First 6 years of her life were spent mainly living at Bara having surgery after surgery
They built a vagina, but no canal
Treated her like a girl and 21 told her she was intersex
She has serious medical issues, including peeing blood
About to do top surgery to transform into man

Crystal: Fighting for the bill of rights to be changed
Crystal Hendricks is a spokesperson for intersex SA who are campaigning to have IGM banned. They have a meeting on the 16th of May to amend the children's act to include the banning of intersex surgery before the age of 12.
She was physically born a girl, but at 15 she never started her period so she went to Tygerburg hospital where she was treated like a science experiment. The one DR told her to cover her face and they took photos of her genitals without asking for her or her mom’s consent. Eventually they figured out that she had no womb or fallopian tubes and instead she had under developed ovaries that may become cancerous operating on their own. Her ovaries were then removed and she was placed on hormones for the rest of her life. Which have meant she has gained excessive weight that she can’t lose. She now still questions whether or not her ovaries ever had to be removed.

Ntsako
35
Born in Zim moved to SA at 10
assigned female @ birth
family didn't have the finances to do any surgery or see doctors so they left her as is
He is now a he and is so grateful that he wasn't "turned into a monster at birth"



Specialist: Head of paediatric endocrinology at red-cross hospital
She openly admits that RC use to perform gender assignment surgery on infants and babies, but they are trying to change the way they now manage patients. They still assign a gender (which is harmful in itself)and may provide non permanent endocrine treatment. But they no longer perform any cosmetic surgery on infants or babies or perform any permanent gender assignment surgery. She was also open about the fact that this is there policy but there are no laws or policies enforcing this and across the country these surgeries are still being performed.
She speaks about the complexities very well and is open that at medical school they are taught the medicine of the time and she was taught that the right thing to do is gender assignment surgery and make a "nice vagina, call her susie and rear a girl"

Potentially one surgeon from KZN that believes intersex infants and babies should be given surgery so that they can live a normal life.

Travel:
CT based Specialist is willing to fly to JHB
So it will just be her flight CT - JHB return

Kimberly
I can do this alone and pay for my cameraman - so one flight

my parents at me down when I was 21.
they sat me down, and said Dimakatso When you were born, you were not like anyone else. You were born with both genitals.

Both Dimeketso Sibidi and Crystal Hendricks are intersex, which means they are born with physical or biological sex characteristics that did not fit societies traditional definitions of male or female. For intersex babies these characteristics may be apparent at birth or emerge later in life, often at puberty. According to global statistics around 1.7% of the population is intersex

Dimeketso
this is what my mom said Dimakatso you were born different... And we were asked, what were your expectations as parents? And my parents said we wanted a girl

Dimektso
I always have flashbacks of seeing my parents as a little child, them leaving the hospital, and I see myself as normal I didn't understand why are my parents always leaving me behind
It's kind of felt like Baragwanath is my home
It's been operation to operation to normalize me, to fix me.
because of the scars I can only tell where the surgeries were and big surgeries, but what are they taking out or taking in? I have no idea. I know of the external it's a penis that was removed

That's where the mess started. They wanted to create a girl out of my body and uhm it messed up my life, to be honest with you.

Do you have your medical records? Have you tried to get your medical records to see what they did?
Yeah, I've tried to get my medical reports
I went to Baragwanath and they couldn't find my things from the database.
No records, no nothing of Dimakatso.

According to Crystal who is the chairperson of Intersex South Africa Gender alignment surgery on infants and babies is still practiced in South Africa and around the world

The normal standard practice is that if there is an intersex child born and they have ambiguous genitalia or just doesn't fit typical binary notions of male and female, they have to fix it and they have to decide agenda for the child. The only problem is that it's very difficult to get that statistics because it happens in a hospital. It happens with a doctor. And it's just not public information.
currently, if we look at the members up in South Africa, we ONLY have one person that didn't have surgery,

Michelle:
In the past, we thought if you call a little girl, a girl, one individual, a girl, we call you a girl and we make what you see in your panties look like a girl, that you will be a happy and comfortable girl.
We subsequently learned that that was absolutely wrong

link: Dr Michelle Carrihill is the head of paediatric endocrinology at the red cross memorial hospital in Cape town

MICHELLE:
But can we conclusively say that these gender assignments are not happening in South Africa?
I can't I can't tell you that they aren't surgeons out there doing it.
I can tell you that my surgeons aren't
Tygerberg signage
Crystal walking at Tygerberg

In 2004 Crystal went to Tygerberg hospital because was 17-years-old and had not yet started her period. And even though the doctors did extensive tests, that resulted in surgery. They never told her or her family that she was intersex




CRYSTAL:
the doctor told my mother Mrs. Schoeman, Crystal is born without a womb. She does have internal ovaries. She'll never be able to have children. the doctor said the ovaries need to be removed because if they are working on their own, they can become cancerous.
on the day I went for surgery
the professor that was there throughout the whole process. I don't even know his name anymore he asked me to step from the bed and he asked me to put the robe over my my face.
And when I put the robe over my face, I could hear the sound of a camera going off, like I could hear the click about four clicks. the doctor at that point took pictures of my naked body
I felt like a science project for the professor.
Beat at the swing

VOICE OVER:
Almost 5 years after her surgery Crystal started trying to put the pieces together and went to see a private endocrinologist

the doctor explained to me that for my intersex variation, it's called complete androgen insensitivity syndrome. What that means is that I developed externally as a female. Internally, I had an extra chromosome, no womb, no fallopian tubes, no internal female genitalia, basically, but externally everything looked normal.
AND? that actually it wasn't ovaries, but it was actually testes that I had internally that was removed.

VOICE OVER
According to Carrihill the notion that its better not to let an intersex child know what is happening to their body is outdated and in recent years practices have begun to change

Michelle:
at one stage we thought, you know what, it was kinder for the individual not to let them know they were different don't tell them they're different fix things because make it look normal and then raise them that way and they'll be happy.
So we, again, learned from that. So what we've learned now, it is better to be completely open to completely,

what we do is we explain to the families our investigations and we say we know that children who have this pattern are happier being boys, or we know that children who have this pattern are happier being girls and we will council them and will guide them.
And that's how we assign gender in those cases
And then we asked them to stay open minded because we may still not be right for that baby
And then the next question is usually, when are you going to operate and fix this? And that is when we come in with
even more intensive counselling, to explain to them that we don't do the surgery at this stage because often that's all they want, is they just want it to look like something that it's OK that everybody else would be OK with

Michelle:
the problem with our law is that it does allow if you're competent surgeon who can do the operation and is qualified to do the operation of this register, to do the operation and the parents who are the proxy autonomy of that baby agree to the operation and operation can be done.
so if your baby girl that is now being raised as a girl has a large clitoris and you don't want it there There's no law in South Africa that says it may not be done,

Dimeketso
I wish the medical people could be taught that let intersex people just live the way they are, you know, don't do anything.
You have no right.
I believe with my whole being that nobody has a right to choose a gender for anybody. And with me gender was already chosen for me from heaven and which is being an intersex person
God is the one that created me So if you don't understand God's creation, you can question me.


Claire: So gender activists and intersex activists, their issue is that they want medical professionals to allow an intersex child just to be intersex. So they do not identify either they're not forced to identify either as male or as female,

Michelle: So because we're in a societal stage where binary is still existent
there are girls bathrooms there are boys bathrooms.. They are girls clothes and boys clothes, school uniforms, etc
it might change in the future. But right now, we really do believe that we make the child more able to be comfortable and confident in their society by giving them a gender and allowing them to be comfortable in that gender.

United Nations human rights bodies have increasingly condemned countries around the world for failing to ban medically unnecessary surgery on intersex children.

I don't think I fit anywhere, I don't think I fit with the boys, I don't think I fit with the girls, Jesus, I don't even think I fit with the lesbians. It sounds so lonely. Yes it is

I have daily health complications , especially when it's winter?
bladder problems or most intersex people, they suffer from kidney infection.
and with me it's kidney problems and with my bladder and through the surgeries they did

which is why Intersex South Africa has put in an application to have the childrens bill of rights to protect intersex babies

what we are seeing in the children's book is that surgery only needs to perform. If there's actually a life threatening illnes

what we are trying to do in the child's body is to make sure that the child's voice is not silent, but the child has consent for anything that needs to be done to the body.

Dimeketso
The only thing you got to do as a parent is just love and support your child as they are. And your child is going to love you as you are as a mother.
no surgeries.

Runs an intersex organisation in Kimberly No endocrinologist in the whole area, hasn't seen one since 2017 Garfield: Surgery at Red cross 38 years old Dr's asked parents what do you want a boy or a girl and they said a girl First 6 years of her life were spent mainly living at Bara having surgery after surgery They built a vagina, but no canal Treated her like a girl and 21 told her she was intersex She has serious medical issues, including peeing blood About to do top surgery to transform into man Crystal: Fighting for the bill of rights to be changed Crystal Hendricks is a spokesperson for intersex SA who are campaigning to have IGM banned. They have a meeting on the 16th of May to amend the children's act to include the banning of intersex surgery before the age of 12. She was physically born a girl, but at 15 she never started her period so she went to Tygerburg hospital where she was treated like a science experiment. The one DR told her to cover her face and they took photos of her genitals without asking for her or her mom’s consent. Eventually they figured out that she had no womb or fallopian tubes and instead she had under developed ovaries that may become cancerous operating on their own. Her ovaries were then removed and she was placed on hormones for the rest of her life. Which have meant she has gained excessive weight that she can’t lose. She now still questions whether or not her ovaries ever had to be removed. Ntsako 35 Born in Zim moved to SA at 10 assigned female @ birth family didn't have the finances to do any surgery or see doctors so they left her as is He is now a he and is so grateful that he wasn't "turned into a monster at birth" Specialist: Head of paediatric endocrinology at red-cross hospital She openly admits that RC use to perform gender assignment surgery on infants and babies, but they are trying to change the way they now manage patients. They still assign a gender (which is harmful in itself)and may provide non permanent endocrine treatment. But they no longer perform any cosmetic surgery on infants or babies or perform any permanent gender assignment surgery. She was also open about the fact that this is there policy but there are no laws or policies enforcing this and across the country these surgeries are still being performed. She speaks about the complexities very well and is open that at medical school they are taught the medicine of the time and she was taught that the right thing to do is gender assignment surgery and make a "nice vagina, call her susie and rear a girl" Potentially one surgeon from KZN that believes intersex infants and babies should be given surgery so that they can live a normal life.
